# Tessera: Complete Documentation (llms-full.txt)

> URL: https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/llms-full.txt | Index: https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/llms.txt | Agent Protocol: https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/agents.txt

# Tessera: Multi-Agent Coordination for Git

> Run multiple agents in the same Git repository.

Tessera works on top of your existing Git repository so concurrent AI agents and terminal sessions can share one checkout, work on independent branches, and merge edits at the AST level without manual worktrees or overwritten files.

```ts
// Live Multi-Agent Attribution in src/currency.ts (main):
// [CodeLens] 2 agents concurrently editing this file (main): antigravity-a1b2 · claude-c3d4
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  // [antigravity-a1b2 · L3-L6: Add locale and decimals]
  currency = "USD",
  locale = "en-US",
  decimals = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
// [claude-c3d4 · L10-L14: Add formatCompact helper]
export function formatCompact(cents: number) {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
    style: "currency", currency: "USD", notation: "compact"
  }).format(cents / 100);
}
```

## Why Tessera?

In standard Git, every open terminal and AI agent shares a single `.git/HEAD` and working directory. Running two agents at once overwrites files or forces you to maintain separate `git worktree` folders. Tessera does not replace Git. It coordinates sessions inside `.git/tessera` and writes standard Git commits so you stay in one folder while each session owns its own branch, dev server, and AST-merged changes. [Read Why Tessera? →](/getting-started/why-tessera)

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

### **Semantic Merging**
Line-based Git merges break when two agents edit the same file. Tessera parses your code with Tree-sitter to merge functions, imports, class methods, and manifest files structurally.

```ts
// Agent 1 adds `locale`, Agent 2 adds `decimals` to the same signature:
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  currency: string = "USD",
  locale: string = "en-US",
  decimals: number = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
```

### **Session Isolation**
Each terminal tab and agent session can switch to its own branch without changing `.git/HEAD` for the rest of your workspace. Edits on the same branch combine automatically on disk, while edits on separate branches stay completely isolated.

```bash
# Terminal 1 works on feat/pricing
tes switch feat/pricing

# Terminal 2 works on feat/faq at the same time
tes switch feat/faq
```

### **Instant Sandboxes**
Run builds, tests, and dev servers on any branch without reinstalling dependencies. Tessera clones `node_modules`, `target`, and `.venv` using filesystem copy-on-write and assigns each session its own port and test database.

```bash
# Run builds or dev servers in isolated Copy-on-Write branch sandboxes
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run build
tes exec -b feat/faq -- npm test
```

## Work in Parallel

Run multiple agents on the same branch, split features across branches, or run two dev servers side by side from a single checkout.

### 1. Multiple Agents

```bash
# Initialize Tessera and install AI editor rules
tes init

# Prompt two AI agents in parallel:
# Tab 1: "On branch feat/pricing, build PricingCalculator.vue and add it to App.vue"
# Tab 2: "On branch feat/faq, build TestimonialsFaq.vue and add it to App.vue"

# Check live agent sessions and claimed files
tes radar
```

### 2. Per-Terminal Branches

```bash
# Enable (tes:<branch>) in your shell prompt
tes env --install

# Terminal 1: run feat/pricing on port 3100
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev

# Terminal 2: run feat/faq on port 3200
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
```

### 3. Branch Merging

```bash
# Inspect branch diffs against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
tes diff -b feat/faq

# Merge both branches into main using 3-way AST merge
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"

# Push to remote
tes push
```

---

# Getting Started

Tessera works on top of your existing Git repository so multiple AI coding agents and terminal sessions can work in the same checkout without overwriting files or colliding on `.git/HEAD`. This guide covers installing the `tes` CLI, initializing a repository, and running your first multi-branch workflow.

## Prerequisites

- **OS**: macOS, Linux, Windows, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, or NetBSD
- **Git**: Standard Git 2.23+

## Installation

Install the `tes` CLI on **macOS, Linux, or BSD**:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.sh | sh
tes --version
```

Or on **Windows (PowerShell)**:

```powershell
irm https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.ps1 | iex
tes --version
```

For shell integration, prebuilt binaries, and editor setup details, see the [Installation Guide](/getting-started/installation).

## Initializing Your Project

Navigate to any project directory and run `tes init`:

```bash
tes init
```

This creates `.git/tessera` and installs workspace rules for your AI coding editors.

> **Note:** If the directory is not yet a Git repository, `tes init` runs `git init` and creates an initial commit from your existing files before setting up Tessera.

## Your First Workflow

Switch your current terminal tab to a feature branch, run your tests, and merge your work:

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
npm test
tes status
tes merge feat/pricing --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator"
```

## What Each Command Does

```bash
tes init
```

- Sets up `.git/tessera` inside your existing Git repository
- Installs instruction rules (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/tessera.md`, `.cursor/rules`, `CLAUDE.md`) so your AI coding agents coordinate through Tessera

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
```

- Binds your current terminal tab to the `feat/pricing` branch (creating it from `HEAD` if it does not exist yet)
- Prepares a Copy-on-Write sandbox for `feat/pricing` that shares your existing `node_modules`, `target`, or `.venv`

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator"
```

- Merges `feat/pricing` into `main` using Tessera's 3-way AST merge engine
- Updates your working directory on `main`

## Working in a Single Folder

In standard Git, running two AI agents on two different branches requires creating separate `git worktree` folders, reinstalling dependencies in each folder, and configuring different ports by hand.

With Tessera, you work inside a **single repository folder**:

```bash
# Terminal 1 works on feat/pricing (assigned port 3100)
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev

# Terminal 2 works on feat/faq in the same folder (assigned port 3200)
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
```

When you prompt an AI agent in your editor, you do not need to mention `tes` in your prompt:

```text
On branch feat/pricing, create PricingCalculator.vue and add it to src/App.vue.
```

The workspace rules installed by `tes init` instruct the agent to claim the branch, isolate its edits, verify the build in its branch sandbox, and commit.

## Next Steps

- [Why Tessera?](/getting-started/why-tessera) - See how Tessera compares to standard Git and `git worktree`
- [Installation](/getting-started/installation) - Set up `(tes:<branch>)` in your terminal prompt and tab completion
- [Your First Workflow](/getting-started/first-workflow) - Walk through a multi-agent example step by step
- [Guides](/guides/) - Learn about multi-agent workflows, dev servers, conflicts, and editor integration

# Why Tessera?

Git assumes one person is editing one branch in one folder at a time. Every terminal tab and editor window in your project reads from the same `.git/HEAD` and writes to the same working tree on disk.

That works fine when you write code by hand in a single editor, but it breaks down when you run two or three AI coding agents in parallel.

If two agents edit `src/App.vue` at the same time, the second agent to save overwrites the first agent's lines, or sees unfamiliar code and reverts it. If one agent runs `git checkout feat/pricing` to test its work, it switches the branch underneath your editor, your running dev server, and every other agent in the folder.

The usual workaround is `git worktree`: creating a separate copy of the repository in another folder for every agent. That requires duplicating `node_modules` or `target` directories, waiting on fresh builds, configuring different ports by hand so dev servers do not collide on `localhost:3000`, and jumping between separate editor windows.

## One Folder, Multiple Branches and Dev Servers

Tessera lets multiple agents and terminal tabs work in the **same repository folder** at the same time, either on separate branches or on the same branch.

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

When an agent claims a branch like `feat/pricing`, Tessera isolates that session inside `.git/tessera/` without changing `.git/HEAD` for the rest of your workspace. Both agents can edit `src/App.vue` on their own branches in `~/acme-web` at the same time without touching each other's uncommitted files.

When you want to preview or test a branch, `tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run dev` starts the dev server inside a copy-on-write sandbox. It clones your existing `node_modules`, `target`, or `.venv` directory in milliseconds using filesystem reflinks and assigns each branch its own port (`localhost:3100`, `localhost:3200`) so you can open both branches side by side in your browser.

## Merging by Syntax Tree

Line-based Git merges fail whenever two branches touch adjacent lines, like when two agents add imports at the top of `src/App.vue` or register two new components in the same template.

When you run `tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main`, Tessera parses each file into a syntax tree with Tree-sitter and merges functions, imports, JSX/Vue templates, and lockfiles structurally. Compatible edits merge without manual conflict resolution.

## Editing on the Same Branch

You do not always want separate branches. When two agents work directly on `main` at the same time, Tessera runs a 3-way AST merge on disk every time an agent saves a file.

```text
[Workflow: Same-Branch AST Merging on main]
1. Prompt on main   -> Agent 1 ("Add locale") & Agent 2 ("Add decimals") target src/currency.ts
2. Concurrent Edits -> Both agents save directly on main (no file locks)
3. Tree-sitter AST  -> Parses FunctionDecl -> merges ParamNode[1] (locale) + ParamNode[2] (decimals)
4. Unified on Disk  -> Both edits preserved in src/currency.ts with zero overwrites
```

If one agent updates `formatCurrency()` while another adds `formatCompact()` in `src/currency.ts`, both edits are preserved on disk. In VS Code and Cursor, the Tessera extension highlights each agent's lines so you can see which session owns each change.

## Built on Top of Git, Not a Replacement

Tessera is not a replacement for Git and does not use a hosted server. Instead, it gives each AI agent and terminal session its own isolated state in `.git/tessera/` so concurrent sessions can use Git branches, diffs, and commits safely in the same working directory.

Every `tes commit` or `tes merge` writes standard Git blobs, trees, and commits directly into `.git/objects/` and `refs/heads/*`. Your existing `git push`, GitHub pull requests, and CI pipelines work without changes.

# Installation

This guide covers installing the `tes` CLI, enabling shell prompt integration, and configuring your AI coding editors.

## Requirements

Tessera is lightweight and self-contained:

- **OS**: macOS (APFS), Linux (Btrfs / XFS / bcachefs / ext4), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, or Windows (WSL2 and native Windows with PowerShell / Windows Terminal)
- **Git**: Standard Git 2.23+

> [!INFO]
> On macOS (APFS) and Linux (Btrfs / XFS / bcachefs), Tessera uses native Copy-on-Write filesystem clones (`clonefile` and `FICLONE`) to duplicate `node_modules` and `target` directories in milliseconds without using extra disk space. On ext4, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, and Windows, Tessera automatically falls back to portable recursive sandbox cloning.

## Installing the CLI

### macOS, Linux, and BSD

Install `tes` on macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel), Linux (`x86_64` & `ARM64`, glibc & musl), FreeBSD, or OpenBSD:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.sh | sh
```

### Windows (PowerShell)

Install `tes.exe` on Windows (`x86_64` and `ARM64`) using PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.ps1 | iex
```

The Windows installer verifies the SHA-256 checksum, extracts `tes.exe` into `$HOME\.local\bin`, and adds it to your user `Path`.

### Prebuilt Binaries

You can also download prebuilt archives directly from GitHub Releases:

| Platform                           | Architecture                            | Release Archive                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **macOS**                          | Apple Silicon (`arm64`)                 | [`tes-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz) |
| **macOS**                          | Intel (`x86_64`)                        | [`tes-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz) |
| **Linux**                          | `x86_64` (static musl / glibc)          | [`tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz) / [`tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) |
| **Linux**                          | `ARM64` (`aarch64` static musl / glibc) | [`tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz) / [`tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) |
| **Windows**                        | `x86_64` (MSVC)                         | [`tes-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) |
| **Windows**                        | `ARM64` (MSVC)                          | [`tes-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) |
| **FreeBSD**                        | `x86_64`                                | [`tes-x86_64-unknown-freebsd.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-freebsd.tar.gz) |
| **OpenBSD**                        | `x86_64`                                | [`tes-x86_64-unknown-openbsd.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-openbsd.tar.gz) |
| **VS Code / Antigravity / Cursor** | Universal `.vsix`                       | [`tessera-vscode.vsix`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tessera-vscode.vsix) |

Verify the installation:

```bash
tes --version
```

## Shell Integration

Each terminal tab can switch branches independently, so it helps to show the active branch in your prompt:

```text
~/code/my-app main (tes:feat/pricing) ❯
```

### Automatic Setup

Run `tes env --install` once to configure your shell profiles (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.profile`, `~/.kshrc`, `~/.mkshrc`, `~/.tcshrc`, `~/.cshrc`, Fish's `config.fish`, and PowerShell's `$PROFILE` on Windows) automatically:

```bash
tes env --install
```

Open a new terminal tab (or reload your shell profile) to activate the prompt indicator and `<TAB>` auto-completion for branch names, commit SHAs, and checkpoints.

### Manual Shell Setup

If you prefer to configure your shell manually, add the line matching your shell:

**Zsh (`~/.zshrc`)** (Powerlevel10k, Oh My Zsh, Starship, and default Zsh)

```bash
eval "$(tes env --zsh)"
```

**Bash (`~/.bashrc` or `~/.bash_profile`)** (Bash 3.2+ and 5.x, Starship, Oh My Bash, and default Bash)

```bash
eval "$(tes env --bash)"
```

**Fish (`~/.config/fish/config.fish`)** (Tide, Starship, Hydro, and default Fish)

```bash
tes env --fish | source
```

**POSIX `sh` / `dash` / `ksh` / `mksh` / `oksh` / `yash` (`~/.profile`, `~/.kshrc`, or `~/.mkshrc`)**

```bash
eval "$(tes env --sh)"
```

**`tcsh` / BSD `csh` (`~/.tcshrc` or `~/.cshrc`)**

```bash
eval "`tes env --tcsh`"
```

**Nushell (`~/.config/nushell/config.nu`)**

```bash
tes env --nu | save -f ~/.config/nushell/tes.nu
source ~/.config/nushell/tes.nu
```

**Elvish (`~/.config/elvish/rc.elv`)**

```bash
tes env --elvish >> ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv
```

**PowerShell (`$PROFILE`)**

```powershell
Invoke-Expression (& tes env --pwsh)
```

## Initializing a Repository

Inside any project directory, run:

```bash
tes init
```

By default, `tes init` auto-detects which AI coding tools you use and generates their instruction files and hooks. To target a specific editor, pass `--harness`:

```bash
tes init --harness antigravity
tes init --harness claude
tes init --harness cursor
tes init --harness windsurf
tes init --harness kiro
tes init --harness opencode
tes init --harness codex
tes init --harness vscode
tes init --harness all
```

## Uninstalling Tessera

### 1. Remove Shell Integration

If you configured shell prompt integration (`tes env --install`), remove the `tes env` line from your shell profile:

- **Zsh (`~/.zshrc`)**: remove `eval "$(tes env --zsh 2>/dev/null)"`
- **Bash (`~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`)**: remove `eval "$(tes env --bash 2>/dev/null)"`
- **POSIX `sh` (`~/.profile`, `~/.kshrc`, `~/.mkshrc`)**: remove `eval "$(tes env --sh 2>/dev/null)"`
- **Fish (`~/.config/fish/config.fish`)**: remove `tes env --fish 2>/dev/null | source`
- **`tcsh` / `csh` (`~/.tcshrc`, `~/.cshrc`)**: remove `` eval "`tes env --tcsh`" ``
- **PowerShell (`$PROFILE`)**: remove `Invoke-Expression (& tes env --pwsh)`

### 2. Delete the CLI Binary

**macOS, Linux, and BSD:**

```bash
rm -f ~/.local/bin/tes
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
Remove-Item -Force "$HOME\.local\bin\tes.exe"
```

### 3. Clean Up Repository State (Optional)

Inside any repository where you ran `tes init`, Tessera stores its metadata and sandboxes in `.git/tessera` (and Git hooks that automatically no-op when `tes` is not installed). To remove the local Tessera state from a repository, delete `.git/tessera`.

# Your First Workflow

In this guide, you will initialize Tessera in a project, work across two feature branches in parallel, and merge both branches back into `main`.

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

## 1. Initialize the Repository

Start by running `tes init` in your project root:

```bash
tes init
```

If you have not already enabled shell prompt integration, run:

```bash
tes env --install
```

## 2. Work on Two Branches in Parallel

You can work on multiple branches at the same time by prompting two AI agent tabs or opening two terminal tabs.

### Option A: Prompt Two AI Agents

Open two AI agent chat tabs in your editor and give each one a task on its own branch:

- **Tab 1**: *"On branch `feat/pricing`, create `src/components/PricingCalculator.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*
- **Tab 2**: *"On branch `feat/faq`, create `src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*

### Option B: Use Two Terminal Tabs

Or open two terminal tabs in the same repository and switch each terminal to its own branch:

**Terminal 1:**

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
```

**Terminal 2:**

```bash
tes switch feat/faq
```

> **Tip:** Each terminal tab remembers its own branch without changing `.git/HEAD` for your editor or other terminals.

## 3. Inspect Live Sessions and Changes

At any point, you can view active agent sessions, modified files, and diffs:

```bash
# See all active agent and terminal sessions
tes radar

# List all branches in the repository
tes branch

# View modified files in the current session or branch
tes status

# Compare a specific branch against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
tes diff -b feat/faq
```

### Command Summary

**`tes radar`**
- Shows every active AI agent or terminal session
- Displays each session's target branch, assigned port (`:3100`, `:3200`), and claimed files

**`tes status`**
- **Staged / Session Changes**: Files recorded in the current session (`M`, `A`, `D`)
- **Unstaged Changes**: Working tree edits on disk not yet reconciled
- **Committed on Branch**: Files committed on the feature branch ahead of `main`

**`tes diff -b <branch>`**
- Shows a unified diff comparing `<branch>` against `main` without switching your editor branch

## 4. Merge Both Branches into `main`

When both features are ready, combine them into `main` with a single command:

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator and faq"
```

Even if both `feat/pricing` and `feat/faq` added imports and components to `src/App.vue`, Tessera's 3-way AST merge engine combines both sets of imports and template blocks without conflict markers.

## Key Concepts

### 1. Per-Session Branches

In standard Git, `git checkout feat/pricing` switches the entire folder for every open terminal and AI agent. In Tessera:

- `tes switch feat/pricing` binds only the **current terminal session** to `feat/pricing`.
- `tes claim --branch feat/pricing ...` binds only that **AI agent session** to `feat/pricing`.
- Clicking the branch name in the IDE status bar (or running `tes switch feat/pricing --editor`) switches your **editor working tree** (`repo_root`) so your file explorer displays `feat/pricing`.

### 2. Branch Sandboxes

When you run commands in a switched terminal or via `tes exec -b <branch> -- <cmd>`, Tessera runs the command inside a Copy-on-Write sandbox for that branch:

```bash
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run build
tes exec -b feat/faq -- npm run build
```

Both commands reuse your existing `node_modules` (or `target` / `.venv`).

### 3. Checkpoints and Undo

Every operation in Tessera is recorded in an operation log inside `.git/tessera`. If an agent makes an unwanted change or you want to roll back a merge, run:

```bash
tes undo
```

# Agents

Once a repository is initialized with `tes init`, editors and CLI harnesses like Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro, and OpenCode can work in the same checkout simultaneously without overwriting each other's files.

## Automatic Coordination

You do not need to change how you prompt your AI agents or manually manage locks. The workspace rules installed by `tes init` instruct each agent to run four commands:

```text
[Workflow: How Agents Coordinate Automatically]
1. Claim Task        -> tes claim --branch <branch> --intent "<goal>" <files...>
2. Reconcile Edits   -> tes hook post-tool --path <file>   (3-way AST merge on save)
3. Verify in Sandbox -> tes exec -- npm run build          (CoW sandbox on isolated port)
4. Commit to Git     -> tes commit -m "..." / tes merge    (standard Git commit on branch)
```

1. **Claim the task (`tes claim`)**: Before editing files, the agent declares what it is working on, which files it will touch, and (optionally) which branch it is targeting:
   ```bash
   tes claim --branch feat/pricing --intent "Add pricing calculator" src/components/PricingCalculator.vue src/App.vue
   ```
2. **Reconcile edits (`tes hook post-tool`)**: Immediately after modifying a file, the agent reconciles its edit:
   ```bash
   tes hook post-tool --path src/App.vue
   ```
3. **Verify in a sandbox (`tes exec`)**: To run a compiler, type-checker, or test suite, the agent executes inside its branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox:
   ```bash
   tes exec -- npm run build
   ```
4. **Commit (`tes commit` / `tes merge`)**: When finished, the agent commits its changes cleanly onto its target branch:
   ```bash
   tes commit -m "feat(pricing): add pricing calculator"
   ```

## Same Branch vs. Separate Branches

### Same Branch

When two agents work on the **same branch** (for example, both editing on `main`), Tessera combines their edits automatically using 3-way AST merging:

- **Functions and Methods**: Two agents can add or edit different functions, or add methods to the same `class` or `impl` block, in the same file.
- **Imports and Parameters**: Both agents can add imports to the top of a file or add parameters to the same function signature.
- **Vue and Svelte Components**: Concurrent edits to `<script setup>`, `<template>`, and `<style scoped>` blocks merge cleanly.
- **Manifests and Lockfiles**: Concurrent additions to `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` are merged structurally.

### Separate Branches

When you ask Agent 1 to work on `feat/pricing` and Agent 2 to work on `feat/faq`, both agents may touch shared files like `src/App.vue` or `index.html` at the same time.

Tessera keeps each branch isolated:
- Changes made on `feat/pricing` never leak into `feat/faq`'s sandbox or commit tree.
- Two agents on different branches will never trigger a conflict against each other while building their features.
- When both agents finish, you can inspect each branch independently or merge both into `main` with `tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main`.

## Status and Diffs

Check modified files in your current session or branch with `tes status`:

```bash
tes status
```

`tes status` groups files into three sections:
- **Staged Changes**: Changes recorded in the active session (`M`, `A`, `D`)
- **Unstaged Changes**: Working tree edits on disk not yet reconciled
- **Committed on Branch**: Files committed on the current feature branch ahead of `main`

Use `tes diff` to view line-by-line diffs:

```bash
# View all changes in the current session or working tree
tes diff

# View only staged session changes
tes diff --staged

# View changes for a single file
tes diff src/App.vue

# Compare any branch against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
```

## Live Sessions

To see all active agents and terminal sessions in real time, run:

```bash
tes radar
```

`tes radar` shows each session's ID, assigned port slot, target branch, task intent, and modified files.

## See Also

- [Branches](/guides/branches-and-terminals) - Switching and merging branches
- [Sandboxes](/guides/running-tests-and-servers) - Running builds and dev servers in branch sandboxes
- [Examples](/examples/) - Step-by-step walkthroughs

---

# Branches

In standard Git, all open terminals and editor windows share a single `.git/HEAD`. Running `git checkout feat/pricing` in one terminal switches the branch underneath every other open terminal and AI agent.

Tessera separates **per-terminal branches**, **per-agent branches**, and your **editor branch** so they never step on each other.

```text
[Architecture: Editor, Terminal & Agent Branches in One Folder]
- Editor Working Tree : .git/HEAD stays on main in VS Code / Antigravity IDE
- Terminal Tabs       : tes switch feat/pricing (:3100) | tes switch feat/faq (:3200)
- Agent Branches      : tes claim --branch isolates agent edits inside .git/tessera/
- Switch or Merge     : tes switch <branch> --editor  OR  tes merge ... --into main
```

## Switching Branches

When shell integration is enabled (`tes env --install`), each terminal tab has its own session and can switch branches independently:

```bash
# Terminal 1
tes switch feat/pricing

# Terminal 2
tes switch feat/faq
```

If the target branch does not exist yet, Tessera creates it automatically from `HEAD`.

In a switched terminal tab:
- Your shell prompt displays `(tes:feat/pricing)` so you always see which branch that tab is on.
- Commands you run in that terminal (`npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, `cargo test`) execute inside that branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox while your terminal prompt stays in your project folder.
- Other open terminals and your code editor remain untouched.

## Switching the Editor Branch

When you want your IDE file explorer and language server to display a different branch's files in your main repository folder, switch the editor branch:

- **In VS Code / Antigravity IDE**: Click the branch name in the bottom-left status bar and select the branch from the dropdown.
- **From the CLI**: Pass `--editor` (or `-e`) to `tes switch`:

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing --editor
```

Switching the editor branch updates your repository working tree and `.git/HEAD` while keeping any open terminal tabs pinned to their own branches.

## Assigning an Agent to a Branch

To have an AI agent build a feature on a specific branch without switching your editor away from `main`, name the branch in your prompt:

> *"On branch `feat/faq`, create `src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue` and add it to `src/App.vue`."*

The agent claims the branch automatically:

```bash
tes claim --branch feat/faq --intent "Add Testimonials and FAQ section" src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue src/App.vue
```

When the agent finishes and commits onto `feat/faq`, your `main` working tree remains clean.

## Listing Branches

View all branches in the repository and see which branch your current terminal session is using:

```bash
tes branch
```

Pass `--json` to inspect commit hashes, assigned ports, active sessions, and modified files ahead of `main`:

```bash
tes branch --json
```

## Merging Branches

Combine one or more feature branches into `main` (or any target branch) using `tes merge --into`:

```bash
# Merge a single branch into main
tes merge feat/pricing --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator"

# Merge multiple branches into main at once
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

During `tes merge`, Tessera merges unchanged directories without reading file blobs, detects renamed files across directories, renumbers colliding sequential SQL migrations, merges `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` dependencies structurally, and combines concurrent AST changes with Tree-sitter.

## Pushing to Remotes

Commit any pending session changes and push a branch to your Git remote (`origin`):

```bash
tes push
tes push -u origin feat/pricing
```

## See Also

- [Sandboxes](/guides/running-tests-and-servers) - Running builds and dev servers across branches
- [Conflicts](/guides/conflict-resolution) - Handling conflicts and rolling back merges
- [Editor Support](/guides/ide-extension) - Switching and merging branches in VS Code

# Sandboxes

Running commands on another branch usually requires stashing uncommitted work or maintaining a separate `git worktree` with its own dependencies.

Tessera creates Copy-on-Write branch sandboxes that reuse your existing dependencies and assign each session its own port and test database.

## Running Commands

With shell integration enabled (`tes env --install`), switch a terminal tab to any branch and run your test or build commands directly:

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
npm test
npm run build
```

Open a second terminal tab, switch it to another branch, and run tests there at the same time:

```bash
tes switch feat/faq
npm test
```

Each terminal tab executes against its own branch's files and dependencies without interfering with other tabs.

## Running Dev Servers

To preview two feature branches in your browser at the same time with automatic port isolation, enable `port_isolation`:

```bash
tes config set port_isolation true
```

Then switch each terminal tab to its branch and start your dev server:

**Terminal 1:**

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev
# TES_PORT=3100
```

**Terminal 2:**

```bash
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
# TES_PORT=3200
```

Or run them explicitly with `tes exec -b <branch>`:

```bash
# Terminal 1
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run dev -- --port 3100

# Terminal 2
tes exec -b feat/faq -- npm run dev -- --port 3200
```

## One-Off Commands

Use `tes exec` to run a command inside a branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox without switching your terminal tab:

```bash
# Run on the current session's branch
tes exec -- npm run build

# Run on a specific branch
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run build
tes exec -b feat/faq -- ./node_modules/.bin/vue-tsc -b
```

When `tes exec` runs:
1. Tessera materializes the branch's committed files plus any uncommitted changes for that branch into its sandbox.
2. Dependency and build cache directories (`node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`, `vendor`) are cloned via Copy-on-Write.
3. `<sandbox>/node_modules/.bin`, `<sandbox>/.venv/bin`, and `<sandbox>/vendor/bin` are prepended to `PATH`.
4. Any new or modified source files generated by the command (such as codegen output or lockfile updates) are captured back into the branch state.

## Dependency Caches

Tessera clones and synchronizes dependency and build caches across major ecosystems:

| Ecosystem | Cached Directories |
|-----------|--------------------|
| **JavaScript / TypeScript** | `node_modules`, `.pnpm-store`, `.next`, `.nuxt`, `.svelte-kit`, `.turbo`, `.parcel-cache`, `.vite` |
| **Rust** | `target` (plus shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` support) |
| **Python** | `.venv`, `venv`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.tox` |
| **Go / PHP / Ruby** | `vendor`, `.bundle` |
| **Elixir / Erlang** | `_build`, `deps` |
| **JVM / Swift / C++** | `.gradle`, `build`, `.build`, `cmake-build-debug`, `cmake-build-release` |
| **Zig / .NET / Dart** | `.zig-cache`, `zig-out`, `bin`, `obj`, `.dart_tool` |

> **Tip:** If you run `npm install` in your project root *after* a branch sandbox was already created, Tessera syncs the newly installed `node_modules` into the branch sandbox on the next `tes exec` run.

## Environment Variables

Each session slot (`1`, `2`, `3`, ...) receives non-overlapping environment variables:

| Variable | Slot 1 | Slot 2 | Description |
|----------|--------|--------|-------------|
| `TES_PORT` (`PORT` when `port_isolation = true`) | `3100` | `3200` | Calculated as `base_port + (slot * port_stride)` |
| `TES_BRANCH` | `feat/pricing` | `feat/faq` | Target branch name for the session |
| `TES_DB_NAME` | `tessera_slot_1` | `tessera_slot_2` | Isolated database name for integration tests |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `sqlite:///.../tessera_slot_1.db` | `sqlite:///.../tessera_slot_2.db` | Isolated database connection URL |

To customize `base_port`, `port_stride`, `port_isolation`, or custom environment variable templates, see the [Configuration Guide](/guides/configuration).

---

# Conflicts

Most of the time, Tessera combines concurrent edits automatically using 3-way Tree-sitter AST merging and manifest drivers.

A conflict is recorded **only** when two sessions or branches modify the exact same statement or expression in incompatible ways (for example, both rewriting the same heading or return expression to different strings).

## Resolving in the Editor

When a merge conflict occurs while using the VS Code / Antigravity IDE extension:

1. Tessera writes standard Git conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) into the file.
2. The extension opens the conflicted file in your editor and jumps to the `<<<<<<<` line.
3. Edit the file to keep the code you want, remove the conflict markers, and save (`Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S`).
4. As soon as the file is saved without conflict markers, Tessera resolves the conflict and updates the branch commit.

You can also click **`N Conflicts`** in the bottom status bar to open the **Conflict Resolver** panel and resolve with a single click (`AST Union`, `Keep Ours`, `Keep Theirs`, or `Keep Working File`).

## Inspecting Conflicts

To list any unresolved conflicts in your repository:

```bash
tes conflicts
```

Pass `--json` to inspect the base, ours, and theirs snippets along with the participating session IDs:

```bash
tes conflicts --json
```

## Resolving from the CLI

Resolve a conflicted file using one of four strategies:

```bash
# Combine both sides' AST declarations and statements in order
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy ast-union

# Keep the first session/branch's version
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy ours

# Keep the second session/branch's version
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy theirs

# Use the file as currently edited and saved on disk
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy working
```

## Checkpoints

Before asking an AI agent to perform a large multi-file refactor, save a named checkpoint:

```bash
tes checkpoint before-refactor
```

## Restoring Files

Use `tes restore` (or `tes reset`) to restore a branch or specific files to any checkpoint, commit SHA, `HEAD~N`, or branch:

```bash
# Restore the current branch to a named checkpoint or previous commit
tes restore before-refactor
tes restore HEAD~1

# Restore a specific branch without switching to it
tes restore -b feat/pricing HEAD~1

# Discard uncommitted changes in a specific file
tes restore src/App.vue

# Restore a file from another branch or commit
tes restore --source main src/App.vue
```

## Undo

Every claim, file reconciliation, checkpoint, restore, and merge is recorded in `.git/tessera`.

View recent operations:

```bash
tes oplog
```

Undo the most recent operation (including a merge):

```bash
tes undo
```

Or roll back to a specific operation ID from `tes oplog`:

```bash
tes undo --op <operation-id>
```

## See Also

- [Editor Support](/guides/ide-extension) - Conflict resolver and branch graph
- [tes resolve](/cli/resolve) - CLI command reference
- [tes restore](/cli/restore) - CLI command reference

---

# Editor Support

The Tessera extension for **VS Code** and **Antigravity IDE** provides real-time branch switching, a 2D commit graph, active session monitoring, and one-click conflict resolution.

## Status Bar

When you open a repository initialized with `tes init`, two items appear on the left side of the status bar:

1. **Current Branch (`main`)**: Displays the branch currently checked out in your editor working tree. Click it at any time to switch your editor to another branch.
2. **`Graph` / `N Conflicts`**: Opens the Branch Graph. If any unresolved conflicts exist, this item highlights in red (`N Conflicts`) and opens the Conflict Resolver when clicked.

> **Note:** In workspaces that have not been initialized with `tes init`, the Tessera status bar items stay hidden automatically.

## Live Attribution

When two or more AI agents work on the same file on your active editor branch, the extension highlights each agent's lines in real time:

1. **File Summary CodeLens**: Appears at line 1 whenever two or more agents are concurrently editing the file (`2 agents concurrently editing this file (main): antigravity-a1b2 · claude-c3d4`).
2. **Hunk CodeLens (`Jump to Session`)**: Appears directly above the start line of each agent's modified section (`<agent_id> · L<start>-L<end>: <intent> · Jump to Session`). Clicking the CodeLens focuses the originating integrated terminal tab, terminal multiplexer pane (`tmux`, `WezTerm`, `kitty`), external macOS terminal tab (`Terminal.app`, `iTerm2`), or IDE agent conversation.
3. **Gutter Borders and Line Highlights**: Each agent session receives a distinct 3px left border and line highlight along with a matching marker on the scrollbar overview ruler.
4. **Inline Labels and Hover Cards**: The first line of each agent's section displays an italic inline label (`<agent_id>: <intent>`), and hovering any highlighted line shows a card with the agent ID, branch, line range, task intent, and a clickable **`Jump to Session`** action link.

```ts
// Live Multi-Agent Attribution in src/currency.ts (main):
// [CodeLens] 2 agents concurrently editing this file (main): antigravity-a1b2 · claude-c3d4
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  // [antigravity-a1b2 · L3-L6: Add locale and decimals]
  currency = "USD",
  locale = "en-US",
  decimals = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
// [claude-c3d4 · L10-L14: Add formatCompact helper]
export function formatCompact(cents: number) {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
    style: "currency", currency: "USD", notation: "compact"
  }).format(cents / 100);
}
```

## Branch Graph

Click **`Graph`** in the status bar (or run **`tes: Open Branch Graph`** from the Command Palette) to open the commit graph:

- **Branch Column Headers**: Shows each branch's name, current commit hash, sandbox port, modified file count, and active agent sessions, with action buttons to **Switch**, **Merge**, or **Restore**.
- **Commit History**: Displays the commit history across parallel branch lanes with merge nodes, author names, and timestamps. Conflicted merge nodes are highlighted with a red border and a `Conflict` badge.

## Sidebar Views

Clicking the Tessera icon in the Activity Bar opens three sidebar views (plus a **Branches** view inside the Source Control sidebar):

### Branches
Lists every branch in the repository with its short commit SHA and modified file count ahead of `main`. Expanding a branch lets you:
- Switch your editor to that branch
- Open the branch's assigned dev server (`localhost:<port>`)
- Click any modified file (`M`) to open a side-by-side diff against `main`

### Sessions
Displays all active AI agent and terminal sessions (`antigravity-*`, `claude-*`, `codex-*`, `cursor-*`, `term-*`), their target branch, and their current task intent. Clicking the **Jump to Session** inline button (or running `tes session focus <session-id>` from a terminal) navigates directly to that session's terminal tab, multiplexer pane, or IDE window. Expanding a session shows claimed symbols and modified files.

### Checkpoints
Lists active conflicts alongside saved checkpoints (`tes checkpoint`), with toolbar actions to create a new checkpoint or open the Conflict Resolver.

## Conflict Resolution

When a merge conflict occurs:
1. The extension opens the conflicted file in your editor at the `<<<<<<<` conflict marker.
2. Resolve the conflict by editing the file and saving (`Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S` resolves once markers are removed) or by using the **Conflict Resolver** panel (`AST Union`, `Keep Ours`, `Keep Theirs`, `Keep Working File`).

## See Also

- [Branches](/guides/branches-and-terminals) - How editor branches and terminal branches interact
- [Conflicts](/guides/conflict-resolution) - Resolving conflicts and rolling back changes

---

# Configuration

Tessera includes default settings for JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Python, Go, PHP, Ruby, Elixir, JVM, Swift, C/C++, Zig, .NET, and Dart projects.

You can customize ports, verification gates, Copy-on-Write cache directories, and environment variable templates using either a `tessera.toml` file in your project root or the `tes config` command.

## Quick Start

View the active configuration for your repository:

```bash
tes config show
```

## Configuration File (`tessera.toml`)

To share configuration across your team in version control, create a `tessera.toml` file in your repository root.

### Example Configuration

```toml
trunk_branch = "main"
base_port = 3000
port_stride = 100
port_isolation = true
verify_command = "npm run build"

cow_cache_dirs = [
  "node_modules",
  ".pnpm-store",
  "target",
  ".venv",
  "venv",
  "vendor"
]

extra_bin_dirs = [
  "node_modules/.bin",
  ".venv/bin",
  "vendor/bin",
  "bin"
]

[custom_env]
DATABASE_URL = "postgres://localhost:5432/app_slot_{slot}"
REDIS_URL = "redis://localhost:6379/{slot}"
VITE_PORT = "{port}"
```

## Configuration Options

### Core Settings

#### `trunk_branch`

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"main"`
- **Description:** Default primary branch for the repository.

```toml
trunk_branch = "main"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set trunk_branch main
```

#### `base_port`

- **Type:** `number`
- **Default:** `3000`
- **Description:** Starting port used when calculating isolated session ports (`PORT = base_port + slot * port_stride`).

```toml
base_port = 3000
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set base_port 3000
```

#### `port_stride`

- **Type:** `number`
- **Default:** `100`
- **Description:** Port increment between session slots (e.g., Slot 1 receives `3100`, Slot 2 receives `3200`).

```toml
port_stride = 100
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set port_stride 100
```

#### `port_isolation`

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Description:** When enabled (`true`) or when `TES_PORT_ISOLATION=1` is set in the environment, `tes env` and `tes exec` automatically export `PORT` and framework port environment variables (`VITE_PORT`, `PORT`, `FLASK_RUN_PORT`, etc.) and prepend CLI port-wrapper shims (`TES_SHIM_BIN`) for each session slot.

```toml
port_isolation = true
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set port_isolation true
```

#### `verify_command`

- **Type:** `string | null`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Description:** Optional verification command executed automatically when running `tes merge --verify` or `tes commit --verify`.

```toml
verify_command = "npm test"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set verify_command "npm test"
# or using the shorthand flag:
tes config --verify-cmd "npm test"
```

#### `co_author`

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Description:** When enabled (`true`), appends a `Co-authored-by:` trailer (`Co-authored-by: Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>` by default) to commits created by Tessera (`tes commit`, `tes merge`, `tes resolve`, `tes pull`, and `tes cherry-pick`). Commits always record your active Git/system user as the primary `Author`.

```toml
co_author = true
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set co_author true
```

#### `co_author_trailer`

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>"`
- **Description:** Custom identity used in the `Co-authored-by: <trailer>` line when `co_author = true`.

```toml
co_author = true
co_author_trailer = "Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set co_author_trailer "Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>"
```

#### `pager`

- **Type:** `string | null`
- **Default:** `null` (falls back to `TES_PAGER` -> `GIT_PAGER` -> `git config core.pager` -> `PAGER` -> `less -FRX`)
- **Description:** Terminal pager command used for `tes diff`, `tes log`, `tes oplog`, `tes branch`, `tes stash list`, and any command invoked with `--paginate` when `stdout` is an interactive terminal. Set to `"cat"` or pass `-P` / `--no-pager` to disable paging.

```toml
pager = "less -FRX"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set pager "delta --paging=always"
```

### Sandbox Options

#### `cow_cache_dirs`

- **Type:** `string[]`
- **Default:** `["node_modules", ".pnpm-store", ".next", ".nuxt", ".svelte-kit", ".turbo", ".parcel-cache", ".vite", "target", ".venv", "venv", ".pytest_cache", ".mypy_cache", ".ruff_cache", ".tox", "vendor", ".bundle", "_build", "deps", ".gradle", "build", ".build", "cmake-build-debug", "cmake-build-release", ".zig-cache", "zig-out", "bin", "obj", ".dart_tool"]`
- **Description:** Dependency and build cache directories cloned via Copy-on-Write into every branch sandbox.

Add directories via CLI:

```bash
tes config add-cache-dir .nx .angular
```

#### `extra_bin_dirs`

- **Type:** `string[]`
- **Default:** `["node_modules/.bin", ".venv/bin", "venv/bin", "vendor/bin", "bin"]`
- **Description:** Relative directories inside the branch sandbox prepended to `PATH` during `tes exec`.

Add binary directories via CLI:

```bash
tes config add-bin-dir ./scripts ./tools/bin
```

#### `package_globs`

- **Type:** `string[]`
- **Default:** `["crates/*", "packages/*", "apps/*", "services/*", "libs/*"]`
- **Description:** Monorepo workspace or package glob patterns scanned when discovering nested dependency caches.

Add package globs via CLI:

```bash
tes config add-package-glob "modules/*" "plugins/*"
```

### Environment Variables

#### `[custom_env]`

- **Type:** `table`
- **Default:** `{}`
- **Description:** Custom environment variables injected into `tes exec` and switched terminals. Supports `{slot}`, `{port}`, `{branch}`, and `{agent_id}` placeholders.

```toml
[custom_env]
DATABASE_URL = "postgres://localhost:5432/app_test_{slot}"
APP_URL = "http://localhost:{port}"
```

Set environment templates via CLI:

```bash
tes config set-env DATABASE_URL "postgres://localhost:5432/app_test_{slot}"
tes config set-env APP_URL "http://localhost:{port}"
```

### Repository Trust (`tessera.toml`)

When cloning an external repository that includes a checked-in `tessera.toml`, non-executable settings (`trunk_branch`, `base_port`, `port_stride`, `co_author`, `co_author_trailer`, `cow_cache_dirs`, and safe `custom_env` templates) are loaded automatically.

To prevent untrusted repositories from executing arbitrary commands or overriding system binaries automatically, `verify_command`, `pager`, and `extra_bin_dirs` in `tessera.toml` require explicit repository trust:

```bash
# trust the repository's tessera.toml
tes config trust

# revoke trust for tessera.toml
tes config untrust
```

## See Also

- [tes config](/cli/config) - CLI command reference
- [Sandboxes](/guides/running-tests-and-servers) - How branch sandboxes use cache directories and ports
- [Getting Started](/getting-started/) - Project initialization guide
