# Examples

Step-by-step walkthroughs for working with multiple agents and branches in Tessera.

## Available Examples

- [Same-Branch Editing](/examples/same-branch) - Two agents editing the same function or file on `main`
- [Feature Branches](/examples/parallel-branches) - Building two features on separate branches and merging them into `main`
- [Conflict Resolution](/examples/conflict-resolution) - Handling incompatible edits on the same line using the editor or CLI

## Quick Examples

### Initialize and Configure Shell

```bash
tes init
tes env --install
```

### Switch Terminals to Different Branches

```bash
# Terminal 1
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev

# Terminal 2
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
```

### Merge Multiple Feature Branches into `main`

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

---

# Same-Branch Editing

This example walks through two agents editing the same function in `src/currency.ts` on `main`.

```text
[Workflow: Same-Branch AST Merging on main]
1. Prompt on main   -> Agent 1 ("Add locale") & Agent 2 ("Add decimals") target src/currency.ts
2. Concurrent Edits -> Both agents save directly on main (no file locks)
3. Tree-sitter AST  -> Parses FunctionDecl -> merges ParamNode[1] (locale) + ParamNode[2] (decimals)
4. Unified on Disk  -> Both edits preserved in src/currency.ts with zero overwrites
```

## Starting File

Suppose `src/currency.ts` on `main` contains:

```ts
export function formatCurrency(cents: number, currency: string = "USD"): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(2);
  return `${currency} ${amount}`;
}
```

## Prompting Two Agents

Open two AI agent tabs and give both a prompt that modifies `formatCurrency`:

- **Tab 1**: *"Add a `locale: string = 'en-US'` parameter to `formatCurrency` in `src/currency.ts`."*
- **Tab 2**: *"Add a `decimals: number = 2` parameter to `formatCurrency` in `src/currency.ts`."*

## How It Works

1. Both agents claim `src/currency.ts` against the same starting commit on `main`.
2. Agent 1 writes its edit and runs `tes hook post-tool --path src/currency.ts`.
3. Agent 2 writes its edit and runs `tes hook post-tool --path src/currency.ts`.
4. Tessera parses the base version and both agents' versions using Tree-sitter and merges the parameter list and function body automatically.

## Merged Result

```ts
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  currency: string = "USD",
  locale: string = "en-US",
  decimals: number = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
```

## Committing

Check the status and commit:

```bash
tes status
tes diff
tes commit -m "feat(currency): support locale and decimals parameters"
```

## Next Steps

- [Feature Branches](/examples/parallel-branches) - Isolate two features on separate branches
- [Conflict Resolution](/examples/conflict-resolution) - Handle overlapping edits to the same expression

---

# Feature Branches

This example shows two agents building separate features on `feat/pricing` and `feat/faq` while both modifying `src/App.vue` in the same checkout, then merging both branches into `main`.

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

## Starting File

Suppose `src/App.vue` on `main` starts as:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import HelloWorld from './components/HelloWorld.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <HelloWorld />
</template>
```

## 1. Launch Two Agents on Separate Branches

Open two AI agent chat tabs in your editor:

- **Tab 1 (`feat/pricing`)**:
  > *"On branch `feat/pricing`, create `src/components/PricingCalculator.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*

- **Tab 2 (`feat/faq`)**:
  > *"On branch `feat/faq`, create `src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*

## 2. Branch Isolation

Even though both agents edit `src/App.vue` in the same folder at the same time:

- `feat/pricing` only contains `HelloWorld.vue` and `PricingCalculator.vue`.
- `feat/faq` only contains `HelloWorld.vue` and `TestimonialsFaq.vue`.
- When each agent runs `tes exec -- npm run build`, the build runs inside that branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox (`branches/feat-pricing` and `branches/feat-faq`), so neither branch fails with missing-component errors.

## 3. Preview Either Branch

You can inspect the diff of each branch or switch your editor to preview it:

```bash
# Compare each branch against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
tes diff -b feat/faq

# Or switch your editor working tree to feat/pricing
tes switch feat/pricing --editor
```

## 4. Merge Both Branches into `main`

Combine both branches into `main` with a single command:

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator and testimonials faq"
```

Tessera merges both `<script setup>` import blocks and both `<template>` usages cleanly into `main`:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import HelloWorld from './components/HelloWorld.vue'
import PricingCalculator from './components/PricingCalculator.vue'
import TestimonialsFaq from './components/TestimonialsFaq.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <HelloWorld />
  <PricingCalculator />
  <TestimonialsFaq />
</template>
```

## Next Steps

- [Conflict Resolution](/examples/conflict-resolution) - See what happens when two branches change the exact same line
- [Branches](/guides/branches-and-terminals) - Learn more about branch management

---

# Conflict Resolution

This example shows what happens when two branches modify the exact same line in incompatible ways, and how to resolve the conflict in your editor or from the CLI.

## 1. Creating a Conflict

Suppose `index.html` on `main` has:

```html
<title>My App</title>
```

Now suppose:
- Branch `feat/pricing` changes `<title>` to `<title>Pricing | My App</title>`.
- Branch `feat/faq` changes `<title>` to `<title>FAQ | My App</title>`.

When you merge both branches into `main`:

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: merge pricing and faq"
```

All non-overlapping files and components merge automatically, and Tessera reports `1` conflict on `index.html`.

## 2. Resolving in Your Editor

If you have the VS Code / Antigravity IDE extension installed:

1. `index.html` opens in your editor at the `<<<<<<<` line:
   ```html
   <<<<<<< ours
   <title>Pricing | My App</title>
   =======
   <title>FAQ | My App</title>
   >>>>>>> theirs
   ```
2. Edit the line to what you want:
   ```html
   <title>My App | Pricing and FAQ</title>
   ```
3. Save the file (`Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S`). The extension detects that the conflict markers have been removed and resolves the conflict automatically.

## 3. Resolving from the CLI

You can also inspect and resolve conflicts directly from your terminal:

```bash
# List active conflicts
tes conflicts

# Resolve using the edited file on disk
tes resolve index.html --strategy working

# Or pick one side directly
tes resolve index.html --strategy ours
tes resolve index.html --strategy theirs
```

## Next Steps

- [Conflicts](/guides/conflict-resolution) - Learn about checkpoints, `tes restore`, and `tes undo`
- [Editor Support](/guides/ide-extension) - Explore the Conflict Resolver panel

---

# CLI Commands

The `tes` CLI provides commands for initializing repositories, coordinating multiple AI coding agents, managing per-terminal branches, running sandboxed builds, and merging branches.

## Command Overview

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| [tes init](/cli/init) | Initialize Tessera in a Git repository and install AI editor rules |
| [tes env](/cli/env) | Configure shell prompt integration (`(tes:<branch>)`) and tab completion |
| [tes switch](/cli/switch) | Switch the active terminal session or editor working tree to a branch |
| [tes branch](/cli/branch) | List (`-l`, `-v`), create, rename (`-m`), or delete (`-d`/`-D`) branches and sandboxes |
| [tes claim](/cli/claim) | Claim a task intent, target branch, and file paths for an agent session |
| [tes status](/cli/status) | Show session changes, peer changes on the same branch, and branch commits (`-s/--short/--porcelain`, `-b`) |
| [tes diff](/cli/diff) | Show unified diffs or diffstats (`--stat`, `--name-only`, `--name-status`, `-U`, `-w`) for the session, working tree (`--all`), branch, or `<revA>..<revB>` |
| [tes stash](/cli/stash) | Session-isolated AST stash (`push`, `pop`, `apply`, `list`, `drop`, `clear`) |
| [tes radar](/cli/radar) | Show all active AI agent and terminal sessions in real time |
| [tes exec](/cli/exec) | Run a build, test, or server command inside a branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox |
| [tes merge](/cli/merge) | Semantically merge sessions or multiple feature branches into a target branch |
| [tes cherry-pick](/cli/cherry-pick) | Apply a commit (`<rev>`) onto the active branch via 3-way AST merge |
| [tes commit](/cli/commit) | Commit the active session's changes onto its target branch (`-m`, `--amend`, `--no-edit`, `--author`, `--co-author`) |
| [tes pull](/cli/pull) | Fetch and fast-forward or 3-way AST-merge a remote branch while rebasing sessions |
| [tes push](/cli/push) | Synchronize session changes and push a branch to a Git remote |
| [tes log](/cli/log) | Show commit history with branch refs, patches (`-p`), diffstats (`--stat`), graphs (`--graph`), filters (`--grep`, `-S`, `--author`), and pathspecs (`-- <paths...>`) |
| [tes conflicts](/cli/conflicts) | List unresolved merge conflicts |
| [tes resolve](/cli/resolve) | Resolve a conflicted file using `ast-union`, `ours`, `theirs`, or `working` |
| [tes checkpoint](/cli/checkpoint) | Save a named checkpoint in the operation log |
| [tes restore](/cli/restore) | Restore a branch or specific files to a checkpoint, commit, or branch |
| [tes undo](/cli/undo) | Undo the most recent operation or roll back to a specific operation ID |
| [tes config](/cli/config) | View or update repository configuration settings |
| `tes session focus <id>` | Focus the originating terminal tab, multiplexer pane, or IDE window for an active session |

---

## Global Options

These options can be used with any `tes` command:

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--json` | Emit structured JSON output (never paged) |
| `-P, --no-pager` | Do not pipe output into a pager |
| `--paginate` | Pipe output into a pager when `stdout` is an interactive terminal (even for commands like `tes status` and `tes radar` that do not page by default) |
| `-C, --repo <PATH>` | Run against the repository at `<PATH>` |
| `-V, --version` | Display the `tes` version |
| `-h, --help` | Show help for a command |

By default, `tes diff`, `tes log`, `tes oplog`, `tes branch` (when listing), and `tes stash list` automatically pipe output through a pager (`TES_PAGER` -> `tessera.toml` `pager` -> `GIT_PAGER` -> `git config core.pager` -> `PAGER` -> `less -FRX`) when `stdout` is an interactive terminal. `tes status`, `tes radar`, and `tes conflicts` print directly to the terminal unless `--paginate` is passed.

---

## MCP Server

For AI coding editors that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP), `tes mcp` starts a JSON-RPC 2.0 server over `stdio` exposing the following tools:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `claim` | Claim a task intent, target branch (`branch`), and file/symbol list (`symbols`) |
| `status` | Reconcile edits and return session status and branch state |
| `radar` | Return all active agent sessions, target branches, and claimed symbols |
| `branch` | List, delete (`delete` / `force_delete`), or rename (`rename`) branches |
| `stash` | Session-isolated AST stash (`push`, `pop`, `apply`, `list`, `drop`, `clear`) |
| `pull` | Fetch and fast-forward or 3-way AST-merge a remote branch and rebase sessions |
| `cherry-pick` | 3-way AST cherry-pick a commit (`rev`) onto a target branch |
| `conflicts` | List active structural conflicts with base, ours, and theirs snippets |
| `resolve` | Resolve a conflict using `ast-union`, `ours`, `theirs`, or `working` |
| `checkpoint` | Create a named checkpoint in the operation log |
| `restore` | Restore a branch or file paths to a commit, branch, or checkpoint |
| `undo` | Roll back the latest operation or restore to a specific `op_id` |
| `sync` | Synchronize the current session with the latest branch `HEAD` |
| `merge` | Commit the session or AST-merge multiple branches into a target branch |

---

## Configuration

Tessera projects can be configured via `tessera.toml` or `tes config`.

**See:** [Configuration Guide](/guides/configuration) for complete documentation.

---

# tes init

Initialize Tessera in a project directory and install AI editor rules.

## Usage

```bash
tes init [options]
```

## Options

- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Default trunk branch name (default: `main`).
- `--harness <LIST>` - Comma-separated list of AI editors/harnesses to configure (`antigravity`, `claude`, `cursor`, `windsurf`, `kiro`, `opencode`, `codex`, `vscode`, or `all`).

## Description

The `init` command sets up Tessera inside your project by:
1. Initializing `.git` and creating an initial commit if the directory is not already a Git repository.
2. Creating the `.git/tessera` store and default configuration.
3. Installing workspace rules and MCP configuration for detected or specified AI editors (`.agents/rules/tessera.md`, `.cursor/rules/tessera.mdc`, `.windsurf/rules/tessera.md`, `.kiro/steering/tessera.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/config.toml`, `.codex/hooks.json`) so AI coding agents coordinate through Tessera automatically.
4. Installing lightweight Git `post-commit` and `post-merge` hooks to keep `.git/tessera` synchronized with native `git` commands.

## Examples

```bash
# initialize in current directory (auto-detects AI editors)
tes init

# initialize with a specific default branch
tes init --branch main

# install rules for specific AI editors
tes init --harness antigravity,claude,cursor

# install rules for all supported AI editors
tes init --harness all
```

---

# tes env

Configure shell prompt integration and dynamic `<TAB>` completion.

## Usage

```bash
tes env [options]
```

## Options

- `--install` - Automatically append the shell integration to `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.profile`, `~/.kshrc`, `~/.mkshrc`, `~/.tcshrc`, `~/.cshrc`, `~/.config/fish/config.fish`, and PowerShell's `$PROFILE` on Windows (when present).
- `--zsh` - Output the Zsh integration script.
- `--bash` - Output the Bash (`3.2+` and `5.x`) integration script.
- `--fish` - Output the Fish integration script.
- `--sh` - Output the POSIX `sh` / `dash` / `ksh` / `mksh` / `oksh` / `yash` integration script.
- `--tcsh` / `--csh` - Output the `tcsh` / BSD `csh` integration script.
- `--nu` / `--nushell` - Output the Nushell (`nu`) integration script.
- `--elvish` - Output the Elvish integration script.
- `--pwsh` - Output the PowerShell (`pwsh`) integration script.

## Description

The `env` command configures your shell so each terminal tab displays its active Tessera branch (`(tes:<branch>)`) in the prompt, enables `<TAB>` completion for subcommands, branches, and checkpoints, and routes commands in switched terminals to the active branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox.

Even without `tes env` installed in your shell profile, Tessera automatically isolates terminal tabs across macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, and Windows using terminal session environment variables (`TERM_SESSION_ID`, `ITERM_SESSION_ID`, `TMUX_PANE`, `ZELLIJ_PANE_ID`, `WEZTERM_PANE`, `KITTY_WINDOW_ID`, `GHOSTTY_SURFACE_ID`, `ALACRITTY_WINDOW_ID`, `GNOME_TERMINAL_SCREEN`, `KONSOLE_DBUS_SESSION`, `TILIX_ID`, `WT_SESSION`), POSIX session leader (`getsid(0)`), and Windows console/process tree tracking.

## Examples

```bash
# automatically configure your shell profiles
tes env --install

# evaluate manually in ~/.zshrc
eval "$(tes env --zsh)"

# evaluate manually in ~/.bashrc
eval "$(tes env --bash)"

# evaluate manually in ~/.config/fish/config.fish
tes env --fish | source

# evaluate manually in ~/.profile, ~/.kshrc, or ~/.mkshrc (sh, dash, ksh, mksh, oksh, yash)
eval "$(tes env --sh)"

# evaluate manually in ~/.tcshrc or ~/.cshrc
eval "`tes env --tcsh`"

# save and source in ~/.config/nushell/config.nu
tes env --nu | save -f ~/.config/nushell/tes.nu
source ~/.config/nushell/tes.nu

# append to ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv
tes env --elvish >> ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv

# evaluate manually in PowerShell ($PROFILE)
Invoke-Expression (& tes env --pwsh)
```

---

# tes switch

Switch the current terminal session or the editor working tree to a branch.

## Usage

```bash
tes switch <branch> [options]
```

Alias: `tes checkout <branch>`

## Options

- `-e, --editor` - Switch the primary repository working tree (`repo_root` and `.git/HEAD`) so your IDE displays `<branch>`, and also bind the calling terminal session to `<branch>`.
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Bind a specific agent session ID to `<branch>`.

## Description

By default, `tes switch <branch>` binds your current terminal session to `<branch>` (creating the branch at `HEAD` if it does not exist yet) and materializes its Copy-on-Write sandbox without changing `.git/HEAD` for other open terminals or AI agents.

When `--editor` is passed, `tes switch` updates the primary repository working tree (`repo_root`), `.git/HEAD`, and `.git/index` to `<branch>` and binds the calling terminal session to `<branch>` while preserving isolated sandboxes for all other background terminal sessions.

## Examples

```bash
# switch the current terminal tab to feat/pricing
tes switch feat/pricing

# switch both the IDE working tree (repo_root) and current terminal to feat/pricing
tes switch feat/pricing --editor

# bind a specific agent session to feat/pricing
tes switch feat/pricing --agent antigravity-1
```

---

# tes branch

List, create, rename, or delete branches and their Copy-on-Write sandboxes.

## Usage

```bash
tes branch [branch] [options]
```

Alias: `tes branches`

## Options

- `-l, --list` - List branches.
- `-v, --verbose` - Show the tip commit SHA and subject line for each branch in list mode.
- `-d, --delete` - Safely delete `<branch>` and its Copy-on-Write sandbox (refuses if unmerged or dirty).
- `-D, --force-delete` - Force-delete `<branch>` and its Copy-on-Write sandbox even if unmerged or dirty.
- `-m, --move <NEW_BRANCH>` - Rename `<branch>` (or the current session's branch if omitted) to `<NEW_BRANCH>`, migrating active sessions and its Copy-on-Write sandbox.
- `-e, --editor` - When switching to `<branch>`, also switch the primary repository working tree (`repo_root` and `.git/HEAD`) and bind the calling terminal session.
- `--json` - Output detailed branch metadata including commit SHAs, ports, active sessions, modified files, and the commit graph.

## Description

When run with no arguments (or with `-l` / `-v`), `tes branch` lists all local Git and Tessera branches and highlights the current session's active branch with `*`.

## Examples

```bash
# list all branches
tes branch

# list branches with short commit SHAs and commit subjects
tes branch -v

# safely delete a merged branch and its sandbox
tes branch -d feat/old-experiment

# force-delete an unmerged branch
tes branch -D feat/abandoned

# rename a branch and migrate active sessions
tes branch -m feat/old-name feat/new-name

# inspect detailed branch state as JSON
tes branch --json
```

---

# tes claim

Register a task intent, target branch, and file paths for an AI agent session.

## Usage

```bash
tes claim --intent <TEXT> [options] <files...>
```

## Options

- `--intent <TEXT>` - Concise description of the task being performed.
- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Target branch for the session (created from `HEAD` if it does not exist).
- `--agent <ID>` - Explicit session ID (auto-detected from environment by default).

## Description

AI agents run `tes claim` before modifying files. The command records the starting baseline of each claimed file, binds the session to `--branch` if specified, prepares the branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox, and starts the background file watcher.

## Examples

```bash
# claim files on the current branch
tes claim --intent "Add currency formatter" src/currency.ts

# claim files on an isolated feature branch
tes claim --branch feat/pricing --intent "Build pricing calculator" src/components/PricingCalculator.vue src/App.vue
```

---

# tes status

Reconcile working tree edits and display current session and branch status.

## Usage

```bash
tes status [options]
```

## Options

- `-s, --short, --porcelain` - Give the output in compact `XY <path>` short-format.
- `-b, --branch` - Show the branch and session header (`## <branch> [session: <id>]`) in short-format.
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Inspect status for a specific session ID.
- `--json` - Emit structured JSON output.

## Description

The `status` command snapshots any modified files in the current workspace, reconciles concurrent edits, and reports:
1. **Staged / Session Changes**: Files recorded in the current session (`M`, `A`, `D`).
2. **Peer Session Changes (concurrent on `<branch>`)**: Files modified by other concurrent AI agent or terminal sessions on the same branch, kept strictly isolated from your session's staged list.
3. **Unstaged Changes**: Working tree edits on disk not yet claimed by any session.
4. **Committed on Branch**: Files committed on the active feature branch ahead of `main`.

## Examples

```bash
# show current session and branch status
tes status

# show compact short-format status with branch header
tes status -sb

# output status as JSON
tes status --json
```

---

# tes diff

Display line-by-line unified diffs, diffstats, or changed file lists for the session, working tree, branch, or any commit range.

## Usage

```bash
tes diff [options] [<revA>..<revB> | <revA> <revB>] [--] [<paths...>]
```

## Options

- `--staged, --cached` - Show only staged session changes.
- `--all` - Show all combined working tree edits on disk across all concurrent sessions on the branch.
- `--stat` - Show a diffstat summary of changed files and line counts.
- `--shortstat` - Show only the aggregate line count summary (files changed, insertions, deletions).
- `--numstat` - Show machine-friendly per-file added and deleted line counts.
- `--name-only` - Show only the names of changed files.
- `--name-status` - Show names and status letters (`A`, `M`, `D`) of changed files.
- `-U, --unified <LINES>` - Generate diffs with `<LINES>` lines of context instead of the default `3`.
- `-w, --ignore-all-space` - Ignore all whitespace when comparing lines.
- `--ignore-space-change` - Ignore changes in the amount of whitespace.
- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Compare `<BRANCH>` against `main` without switching branches.
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Show changes for a specific session ID.
- `-- <paths...>` - Restrict the diff to specific files or directories.

## Description

By default, when your session has claimed files, `tes diff` shows only your session's isolated diff (`base_commit -> own_blobs`) so concurrent peer edits do not pollute your diff output. You can pass `--all` to inspect the combined working tree diff, `-b <branch>` to diff a branch against `main`, or `<revA>..<revB>` (or `<revA> <revB>`) to diff any two revisions, branches, or commits.

## Examples

```bash
# diff changes in the current session (or working tree if unclaimed)
tes diff

# show diffstat or changed file names for the current session
tes diff --stat
tes diff --name-status

# diff all combined working tree changes across concurrent sessions
tes diff --all

# diff specific paths or directories
tes diff -- crates/cli/src/main.rs docs/

# compare a feature branch against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing

# diff two revisions or branches (optionally scoped to paths)
tes diff HEAD~1..HEAD --stat
tes diff main..feat/pricing -- src/App.vue
```

---

# tes stash

Session-isolated AST stash for saving and reapplying uncommitted changes without interfering with concurrent agents or other branches.

## Usage

```bash
tes stash [subcommand] [options]
```

## Subcommands

- `tes stash [push] [-m <msg>] [-a <ID>] [paths...]` - Save the current session's (or working tree's) uncommitted changes onto the stash stack and restore the stashed files to the branch base. Optionally pass `<paths...>` to stash only specific files.
- `tes stash pop [index] [-a <ID>]` - 3-way AST-merge `stash@{index}` (default `0`) onto the current branch/session and remove it from the stash stack.
- `tes stash apply [index] [-a <ID>]` - 3-way AST-merge `stash@{index}` (default `0`) onto the current branch/session while keeping it in the stash stack.
- `tes stash list` - List all stash entries (`stash@{0}`, `stash@{1}`, ...).
- `tes stash drop [index]` - Delete a single stash entry (default `0`).
- `tes stash clear` - Remove all entries from the stash stack.

## Examples

```bash
# stash all changes in the current session or working tree
tes stash -m "WIP: refactor billing"

# stash only specific files while keeping other edits in place
tes stash push -m "partial stash" src/billing.ts

# list stashes
tes stash list

# pop the most recent stash via 3-way AST merge
tes stash pop

# apply stash@{1} without dropping it
tes stash apply 1
```

---

# tes radar

Display all active AI agent and terminal sessions in real time.

## Usage

```bash
tes radar [options]
```

## Options

- `--json` - Emit structured JSON output.

## Description

`tes radar` shows every active session in the repository along with its assigned slot number, target branch, task intent, claimed AST symbols, and modified files. Any structural overlaps between sessions on the same branch are highlighted.

## Examples

```bash
# inspect live sessions
tes radar

# output live sessions as JSON
tes radar --json
```

---

# tes exec

Run a command inside an isolated Copy-on-Write branch sandbox.

## Usage

```bash
tes exec [-b <branch>] -- <command...>
```

## Options

- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Target branch sandbox to run the command in (defaults to the current session's branch).
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Explicit session ID.

## Description

`tes exec` materializes the target branch's files into a Copy-on-Write sandbox, clones dependency and build caches (`node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`, `vendor`), prepends `<sandbox>/node_modules/.bin` to `PATH`, and exports isolated `PORT`, `TES_PORT`, `TES_BRANCH`, and `DATABASE_URL` environment variables.

## Examples

```bash
# run a build on the current session's branch
tes exec -- npm run build

# run a build on a specific branch without switching your working tree
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run build

# run tests on two branches in parallel
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm test
tes exec -b feat/faq -- npm test
```

---

# tes merge

Commit the current session or semantically merge multiple branches into a target branch.

## Usage

```bash
tes merge [branches_or_sessions...] [options]
```

## Options

- `--into <BRANCH>` - Target branch to merge into (defaults to the active session's branch or `main`).
- `-m, --message <MSG>` - Commit message for the merge commit.
- `--verify <CMD>` - Verification command to run before finalizing the merge.
- `--keep-open` - Keep agent sessions open after merging.
- `--co-author [=<NAME <EMAIL>>]` - Append a `Co-authored-by:` trailer to the merge commit (defaults to configured `co_author_trailer` when passed without a value; repeatable).
- `--no-co-author` - Omit `Co-authored-by:` trailers even if `co_author = true` in repository config.
- `--author <NAME <EMAIL>>` - Override the commit `Author` identity for the merge commit.

## Description

When called with `-m "<message>"` inside an active session, `tes merge` commits the session's changes onto its target branch.

When called with one or more branch names and `--into <target>`, `tes merge` combines the branches into `<target>` using Tessera's semantic merge pipeline (subtree skipping, rename detection, SQL migration resequencing, manifest drivers, and 3-way Tree-sitter AST merging).

Merge commits record your active Git/system user as the commit `Author` (or `--author "Name <email>"` when specified), and optionally append `Co-authored-by: Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>` when `co_author = true` is configured (`false` by default) or `--co-author` is passed.

## Examples

```bash
# commit the current session onto its target branch
tes merge -m "feat(pricing): add pricing calculator"

# merge two feature branches into main
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"

# merge with an explicit Co-authored-by trailer
tes merge feat/pricing --into main -m "feat: add pricing" --co-author

# run a verification command before completing the merge
tes merge feat/pricing --into main --verify "npm run build" -m "feat: add pricing"
```

---

# tes cherry-pick

Apply the changes introduced by an existing commit onto the active (or specified) branch via 3-way AST merge.

## Usage

```bash
tes cherry-pick <commit> [options]
```

## Options

- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Target branch to apply the commit onto (defaults to the current session's active branch).
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Explicit session ID.

## Description

`tes cherry-pick` takes the diff introduced by `<commit>` (a commit SHA, branch name, `HEAD~N`, or checkpoint) against its parent and applies it onto the target branch using Tessera's 3-way Tree-sitter AST merge engine, rebasing active sessions on that branch automatically.

## Examples

```bash
# cherry-pick a commit onto the active branch
tes cherry-pick 4beccce

# cherry-pick the tip commit of another branch onto main
tes cherry-pick feat/pricing --branch main
```

---

# tes commit

Commit the current session's changes onto its target branch.

## Usage

```bash
tes commit [-m <MESSAGE>] [options]
```

## Options

- `-m, --message <MSG>` - Commit message.
- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Explicit target branch override.
- `--amend` - Amend the tip commit of the target branch instead of creating a new child commit.
- `--no-edit` - Reuse the previous commit message when amending without `-m`.
- `--verify <CMD>` - Run a verification command before committing.
- `--co-author [=<NAME <EMAIL>>]` - Append a `Co-authored-by:` trailer to this commit (defaults to configured `co_author_trailer` when passed without a value; repeatable).
- `--no-co-author` - Omit `Co-authored-by:` trailers for this commit even if `co_author = true` in repository config.
- `--author <NAME <EMAIL>>` - Override the commit `Author` identity for this commit.
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Explicit session ID.

## Description

`tes commit` snapshots any pending changes in the current session, writes a new commit onto the session's target branch (`refs/heads/<branch>`), and updates the branch sandbox. Passing `--amend` replaces the tip commit on the target branch while preserving its parent commits (and reusing the previous commit message and author when `-m` / `--author` are omitted).

Commits record your active Git/system user (`git config user.name` and `user.email`, with automatic OS user fallback) as the commit `Author`, unless overridden via `--author "Name <email>"`. If `co_author = true` is enabled in `tessera.toml`, via `tes config set co_author true` (`false` by default), or per-commit via `--co-author`, Tessera appends `Co-authored-by: Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>` (or your custom trailer) to the commit message.

## Examples

```bash
# commit changes in the current session
tes commit -m "feat(pricing): add interactive pricing calculator"

# amend the previous commit with new edits or an updated message
tes commit --amend --no-edit
tes commit --amend -m "feat(pricing): add interactive pricing calculator and unit tests"

# commit to a specific branch
tes commit -b feat/pricing -m "feat(pricing): add interactive pricing calculator"

# include the default Co-authored-by trailer on a single commit
tes commit -m "feat(pricing): add tier selector" --co-author

# include a custom Co-authored-by trailer or override the commit author
tes commit -m "feat(pricing): pair on billing logic" --co-author "Alice <alice@example.com>"
tes commit -m "fix(auth): token refresh" --author "Jane Doe <jane@example.com>"
```

---

# tes pull

Fetch from a Git remote, fast-forward or 3-way AST-merge the remote branch into your local branch, and rebase active sessions on that branch.

## Usage

```bash
tes pull [remote] [branch]
```

## Arguments

- `[remote]` - Git remote name (defaults to `origin`).
- `[branch]` - Branch name to pull (defaults to the current session's active branch).

## Description

`tes pull` fetches the latest commits from `<remote>/<branch>`, fast-forwards your local branch ref when possible (or performs a 3-way AST merge if local commits have diverged), and rebases any active sessions and Copy-on-Write branch sandboxes onto the updated branch `HEAD`.

## Examples

```bash
# pull the current active branch from origin
tes pull

# pull a specific branch from origin
tes pull origin feat/pricing
```

---

# tes push

Synchronize pending session changes and push a branch to a Git remote.

## Usage

```bash
tes push [remote] [branch] [options]
```

## Options

- `-m, --message <MSG>` - Commit message if uncommitted session changes need to be committed before pushing.
- `-f, --force` - Push with `--force-with-lease`.
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Explicit session ID.

## Description

`tes push` commits any uncommitted changes in the current session onto the active branch and runs `git push -u <remote> refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>`.

## Examples

```bash
# push the active branch to origin
tes push

# push a specific branch to origin
tes push origin feat/pricing
```

---

# tes log

Show the commit history for the active session's branch, any specified branch or revision range, or specific file paths.

## Usage

```bash
tes log [options] [<revision-or-range>] [-- <paths...>]
```

## Options

- `-n, --limit, --max-count <N>` - Maximum number of commits to display (default: `20`).
- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Branch or revision to inspect (defaults to the active session's branch).
- `--oneline` - Display each commit on a single compact line (`<short_sha> (<refs>) <subject>`).
- `-p, -u, --patch` - Generate a unified diff patch for each commit.
- `--stat` - Show a diffstat summary of modified files and line counts for each commit.
- `--name-only` - Show only the names of changed files for each commit.
- `--name-status` - Show the names and status letters (`A`, `M`, `D`) of changed files for each commit.
- `--graph` - Draw a text-based graphical representation of the commit history.
- `--all` - Show commits across all branches and refs.
- `--author <PATTERN>` - Filter commits by author name or email pattern.
- `--grep <PATTERN>` - Filter commits whose commit message matches `<PATTERN>`.
- `-S, --pickaxe <STRING>` - Filter commits that introduce or remove `<STRING>` in the patch.
- `--since, --after <DATE>` - Show commits more recent than a specific date.
- `--until, --before <DATE>` - Show commits older than a specific date.
- `--reverse` - Output the chosen commits in reverse chronological order.
- `-a, --agent <ID>` - Inspect commit history for a specific session's branch.
- `-- <paths...>` - Restrict commit history (and patches) to commits touching the given files or directories.
- `--json` - Emit structured JSON commit entries.

## Examples

```bash
# show recent commits on the current branch
tes log

# show compact one-line commit log
tes log --oneline -n 10

# show the last 4 commits with patches scoped to docs/
tes log -p -n 4 -- docs/

# show diffstat and commit graph across all branches
tes log --graph --stat --all -n 15

# filter commits by message or pickaxe string
tes log --grep "AST" -n 5
tes log -S "merge_trees_3way" --oneline

# inspect commit history of another branch without switching
tes log -b feat/pricing --oneline
```

---

# tes conflicts

List unresolved merge conflicts in the repository.

## Usage

```bash
tes conflicts [options]
```

## Options

- `--json` - Emit structured JSON output with `base`, `ours`, and `theirs` code snippets and participating session IDs.

## Description

`tes conflicts` lists all files that currently have an unresolved structural merge conflict.

## Examples

```bash
# list unresolved conflicts
tes conflicts

# inspect full conflict snippets as JSON
tes conflicts --json
```

---

# tes resolve

Resolve a merge conflict in a file using a specified strategy.

## Usage

```bash
tes resolve <path> --strategy <strategy>
```

## Options

- `--strategy <STRATEGY>` - Resolution strategy (`ast-union`, `ours`, `theirs`, `working`, or `content`).

## Description

The `resolve` command clears the conflict record for `<path>`, writes the chosen resolution to disk and the target branch, and replaces any intermediate conflict commit cleanly:

- `ast-union` - Combine both sides' AST declarations and statements in order.
- `ours` - Keep the first session or branch's version.
- `theirs` - Keep the second session or branch's version.
- `working` - Use the file as currently edited and saved on disk.

## Examples

```bash
# combine both sides using AST union
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy ast-union

# keep the first branch's version
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy ours

# keep the second branch's version
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy theirs

# resolve using the manually edited file on disk
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy working
```

---

# tes checkpoint

Save a named checkpoint in the operation log.

## Usage

```bash
tes checkpoint <name>
```

## Arguments

- `<name>` - Name for the checkpoint (e.g., `before-refactor`).

## Description

`tes checkpoint` snapshots the current working tree and session state and records a named checkpoint in `.git/tessera`. You can restore the repository back to this checkpoint at any time using `tes restore <name>`.

## Examples

```bash
# save a named checkpoint
tes checkpoint before-refactor

# restore back to the checkpoint later
tes restore before-refactor
```

---

# tes restore

Restore a branch or specific files to a checkpoint, commit, or branch.

## Usage

```bash
tes restore [options] [target_or_paths...]
```

Alias: `tes reset`

## Options

- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` - Restore a specific branch without switching your working tree to it first.
- `-s, --source <REF>` - Restore specific files from `<REF>` (checkpoint name, commit SHA, `HEAD~N`, or branch name).

## Description

When given a checkpoint name, commit SHA, or `HEAD~N` (with no file paths), `tes restore` resets the target branch to that point in time and synchronizes `.git/HEAD`, `.git/index`, active agent baselines, and the branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox.

When given file paths, `tes restore` restores only those files from `--source` (or from `HEAD` if `--source` is omitted).

## Examples

```bash
# restore the current branch to a named checkpoint or previous commit
tes restore before-refactor
tes restore HEAD~1

# restore a specific branch to its previous commit
tes restore -b feat/pricing HEAD~1

# discard uncommitted changes in a file
tes restore src/App.vue

# restore a file from main
tes restore --source main src/App.vue
```

---

# tes undo

Undo the most recent operation or roll back to a specific operation ID.

## Usage

```bash
tes undo [options]
```

## Options

- `--op <OP_ID>` - Roll back to a specific operation ID from `tes oplog`.
- `--checkpoint <LABEL>` - Roll back to a named checkpoint created with `tes checkpoint <LABEL>`.

## Description

Every state change in `.git/tessera` is recorded in the operation log (`tes oplog`). Running `tes undo` reverses the most recent operation and restores the working tree and branch refs to their prior state.

## Examples

```bash
# view recent operations
tes oplog

# undo the most recent operation
tes undo

# roll back to a specific operation ID
tes undo --op 8f3a1c2

# roll back to a named checkpoint
tes undo --checkpoint before-refactor
```

---

# tes config

View or update repository configuration settings.

## Usage

```bash
tes config <subcommand> [arguments]
```

## Subcommands

- `show` - Display the effective configuration for the repository.
- `set <KEY> <VALUE>` - Update `trunk_branch`, `base_port`, `port_stride`, `port_isolation`, `verify_command`, `watch_interval_ms`, `watch_timeout_secs`, `co_author`, `co_author_trailer`, `auto_isolate_dirty_claims`, or `pager`.
- `trust` - Trust the repository's `tessera.toml` so `verify_command`, `pager`, `extra_bin_dirs`, and `custom_env` defined in `tessera.toml` are allowed to execute.
- `untrust` - Revoke trust for the repository's `tessera.toml`.
- `add-cache-dir <DIRS...>` - Add directories to `cow_cache_dirs`.
- `add-bin-dir <DIRS...>` - Add directories to `extra_bin_dirs`.
- `add-package-glob <GLOBS...>` - Add monorepo package glob patterns to `package_globs`.
- `set-env <KEY> <TEMPLATE>` - Set a custom environment variable template (`{slot}`, `{port}`, `{branch}`, `{agent_id}`).

## Options

- `--verify-cmd <CMD>` - Shorthand to set `verify_command` directly (`tes config --verify-cmd "npm test"`).

## Examples

```bash
# view current configuration
tes config show

# update base port, port isolation, and verification command
tes config set base_port 3000
tes config set port_isolation true
tes config set verify_command "npm test"

# enable Co-authored-by trailer on Tessera commits (false by default)
tes config set co_author true

# configure a custom terminal pager (e.g. delta or less -FRX)
tes config set pager "delta --paging=always"

# trust a cloned repository's tessera.toml
tes config trust

# add a Copy-on-Write cache directory
tes config add-cache-dir .nx

# set a custom environment variable template
tes config set-env DATABASE_URL "postgres://localhost:5432/app_slot_{slot}"
```

## See Also

- [Configuration Guide](/guides/configuration) - Full `tessera.toml` reference
